rules.name: hh.exe opens a remote or user-writable CHM
rules.description: HTML Help is pointed at a URL or a .chm in a temp, downloads or public folder, a compiled-HTML execution route.

rules.name: cmstp.exe installs an INF silently
rules.description: cmstp runs with /s (silent) and an INF file, often with /ns, the known profile-installer proxy-execution pattern.

rules.name: odbcconf.exe loads a DLL through a response file or REGSVR
rules.description: odbcconf with /a {REGSVR dll} or a /f response file executes a DLL, a signed-binary proxy route.

rules.name: XSL script processed by wmic or msxsl from a remote or user path
rules.description: wmic /format or msxsl loads an XSL stylesheet from a URL or user-writable path, which can embed script.

rules.name: Office application opens a remote template
rules.description: An Office program is launched with a URL to a .dot/.dotm/.dotx template, the remote template injection delivery pattern.

rules.name: netsh add helper registers a helper DLL
rules.description: netsh add helper installs a DLL that netsh loads on every start, persistence through helper DLLs.
rules.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Netsh Helper DLL

rules.name: NetSh helper key value set
rules.description: A value is written under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\NetSh, which lists helper DLLs netsh loads.
rules.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Netsh Helper DLL

rules.name: Accessibility binary gets an IFEO debugger
rules.description: A Debugger value is set under Image File Execution Options for sethc, utilman, osk, narrator, magnify or displayswitch, the sticky-keys backdoor.

rules.name: Accessibility binary overwritten with a shell
rules.description: A copy or takeown/icacls command targets sethc, utilman, osk or narrator in System32, the file-replacement variant of the sticky-keys backdoor.

rules.name: reg.exe writes AppCertDLLs
rules.description: reg add targets the Session Manager AppCertDLLs key, which loads a DLL into every process using CreateProcess.

rules.name: emond rule file created
rules.description: A plist is created under /etc/emond.d/rules or /private/var/db/emondClients; emond runs actions from these on system events.

rules.name: COM InprocServer32 set to a user-writable DLL
rules.description: A CLSID InprocServer32 or LocalServer32 default value points into a user-writable directory, the COM hijacking persistence pattern.
rules.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Component Object Model Hijacking

rules.name: reg.exe edits LSA Security Packages
rules.description: reg add of Security Packages or Authentication Packages under Control\Lsa registers a DLL the LSA loads, a credential-theft persistence route.
rules.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Security Support Provider

positive.command: reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v Security Packages /d mimilib /t REG_MULTI_SZ

rules.name: mimilib or known SSP DLL loaded
rules.description: A module named mimilib.dll or mimikatz-related SSP loaded by a process; mimilib is the Mimikatz SSP.
rules.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Security Support Provider

rules.name: Shortcut or script created in a Startup folder
rules.description: A .lnk or .url shortcut is created in a user or all-users Startup folder, which runs it at logon. Installers do this too, so informational.

rules.name: Print processor registered
rules.description: A value is set under a Print Processors key, which loads a DLL into the spooler service.
rules.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Print Processors

rules.name: macOS login or logout hook set
rules.description: defaults write com.apple.loginwindow LoginHook or LogoutHook registers a script run as root at login.
rules.technique_name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Logon Script (Mac)

rules.name: StartupItems entry created
rules.description: A file is created under /Library/StartupItems, a legacy macOS autostart location that is rarely used today.
rules.technique_name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Startup Items

rules.name: at job scheduled
rules.description: The at command schedules a one-shot job (now, a clock time, noon or midnight). Routine for admins, so informational.

rules.name: systemd timer unit created
rules.description: A .timer unit is created in /etc/systemd/system or a user systemd directory. Packages and admins do this, so informational.

rules.name: kubectl creates a CronJob or Job
rules.description: kubectl create cronjob or job creates a scheduled workload; admins and CI do it too.

positive.command: kubectl create cronjob beat --image=alpine --schedule='*/5 * * * *' -- sh -c id

rules.name: osascript password prompt with hidden answer
rules.description: osascript display dialog with hidden answer and a password-like prompt, a GUI credential-harvesting pattern.

positive.command: osascript -e 'display dialog \"Enter your password to update\" default answer \"\" with hidden answer'

rules.name: PowerShell credential prompt
rules.description: PromptForCredential or Get-Credential with a spoofed message, a GUI credential-harvest pattern.

rules.name: Known privilege-escalation exploit tool name
rules.description: Command line names a well-known local privilege-escalation exploit or potato tool (PrintSpoofer, JuicyPotato, GodPotato, PwnKit, DirtyPipe, DirtyCow). Name-based, so trivially evaded.

rules.name: Local administrator group enumeration
rules.description: net localgroup administrators, Get-LocalGroupMember, getent group sudo or dscl reading the admin group. Common in admin work, so informational.

rules.name: Secure deletion of logs, history or free space
rules.description: shred of log or history files, sdelete, or cipher /w. Anti-forensic file deletion; admins also use these for data hygiene.

rules.name: NTFS USN journal deleted
rules.description: fsutil usn deletejournal removes file-change history that forensic tools rely on.

rules.name: PowerShell posts data to a raw IP web endpoint
rules.description: Invoke-WebRequest/Invoke-RestMethod or WebClient POST/upload to an http(s) URL with an IP literal host, a basic C2 or exfil web channel.

rules.name: Outbound connection to a common C2 framework port
rules.description: Destination port is 4444, 50050, 31337 or 1337 on a non-private destination: default ports for Metasploit handlers, Cobalt Strike team servers and similar. Port-only heuristic.

rules.name: Successful login by a default or guest account
rules.description: A successful authentication by guest, defaultaccount, support_388945a0 or similar built-in accounts that are normally disabled.

rules.name: runas with /savecred
rules.description: runas /savecred /user: stores and reuses a local or domain account's credentials for execution as that account.

rules.name: Cloud CLI configured with static credentials
rules.description: az login --service-principal, gcloud auth activate-service-account or aws configure set of an access key: a cloud account becomes usable from this host. Routine for automation, so informational.

rules.name: Domain account enumeration
rules.description: net user /domain, dsquery user, Get-ADUser -Filter * or an ldapsearch for user objects lists directory accounts.

rules.name: netsh port proxy configured
rules.description: netsh interface portproxy add relays a listening port to another host and turns the machine into an internal proxy.

positive.command: netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=8080 connectaddress=10.0.0.9 connectport=80

rules.name: Tor or proxychains traffic relay started
rules.description: tor, torify or proxychains runs on the host, routing traffic through multiple hops.

rules.name: User added to a privileged local group
rules.description: usermod/gpasswd/adduser adding to sudo, wheel, admin, docker or root; net localgroup administrators /add; dseditgroup adding to admin.

rules.name: Additional cloud credential created
rules.description: aws iam create-access-key, az ad sp/app credential reset or gcloud iam service-accounts keys create adds a new secret for an existing identity.

positive.command: gcloud iam service-accounts keys create k.json --iam-account s@p.iam.gserviceaccount.com

rules.name: Cluster-admin or broad role bound
rules.description: kubectl create clusterrolebinding/rolebinding to cluster-admin, admin or edit grants broad cluster rights.
rules.technique_name: Account Manipulation: Additional Container Cluster Roles

rules.name: Script fetched from a paste or raw-content service and piped to an interpreter
rules.description: curl/wget/iwr to pastebin raw, gist, raw.githubusercontent or similar piped to sh/bash/python or iex.

rules.name: Command line talks to a chat-bot API for tasking and reply
rules.description: A command uses Telegram bot getUpdates/sendMessage or a Discord/Slack webhook, a bidirectional chat-service C2 pattern.

rules.name: Online password-guessing tool run
rules.description: hydra, medusa, ncrack, patator or crackmapexec with a password list targets a remote service.

rules.name: Offline password-cracking tool run
rules.description: hashcat or john runs with a hash mode or wordlist against a hash file.

rules.name: reg add disables admin tools or policy UI
rules.description: reg add sets DisableTaskMgr, DisableRegistryTools, DisableCMD, NoControlPanel or similar policy values to 1, hindering response.

rules.name: Domain or directory account created from the command line
rules.description: net user /add /domain, New-ADUser, dsadd user or ldapadd of a user creates a directory account.

rules.name: Cloud user or service account created
rules.description: aws iam create-user, az ad user create or gcloud iam service-accounts create via CLI. Routine in provisioning, so informational.

positive.command: az ad user create --display-name x --user-principal-name x@y.com --password p

rules.name: Add-in or template dropped in an Office startup folder
rules.description: A .dotm/.wll/.xlam/.xll file is created in Word STARTUP or Excel XLSTART, which Office loads on every start.
rules.technique_name: Office Application Startup: Office Template Macros

rules.name: Browser started with --load-extension
rules.description: Chromium-based browser launched with --load-extension pointing at an unpacked extension, outside the store.

rules.name: Indirect command execution via forfiles, pcalua or scriptrunner
rules.description: forfiles /c, pcalua -a or scriptrunner -appvscript launch another command without cmd or PowerShell as the visible parent.

rules.name: Document reader spawns a shell or script host
rules.description: A PDF or document reader (Acrobat, Reader, Foxit, Sumatra) has a command interpreter or script host as its child, typical of a client-side exploit.

rules.name: Executable run from an archive viewer temp extraction
rules.description: A process image is located in a Temp folder created by an archive viewer (Temp1_*.zip, Rar$*, 7z*), meaning it was run straight out of an opened archive.

rules.name: Mail or chat client launches a browser to an IP-literal URL
rules.description: Outlook, Thunderbird, Teams or Word is the parent of a browser opened on an http(s) URL with an IP-address host, a malicious-link click pattern.

rules.name: Bulk extraction from a wiki or document repository API
rules.description: curl/wget/python hitting a Confluence or SharePoint REST search/content endpoint with a large limit or CQL query, pulling repository content in bulk.

rules.name: Filesystem search for key, vault or credential files
rules.description: find/dir/Get-ChildItem sweeping for kdbx, pfx, p12, ppk, ovpn or id_rsa files.

rules.name: Impacket remote-execution script run
rules.description: psexec.py, smbexec.py, wmiexec.py, atexec.py or dcomexec.py executed: remote command execution over several remote-service protocols.

rules.name: PowerShell command rebuilt from character codes or XOR
rules.description: A PowerShell command combines [char] code concatenation, or -bxor decoding with FromBase64String/-join, to rebuild a payload.

rules.name: Command line obfuscated with carets or PowerShell backticks
rules.description: Sequences of single characters separated by carets in cmd, or letters broken up by backticks in PowerShell.

rules.name: Compiler writes a binary into a world-writable or shared-memory path
rules.description: gcc/cc/clang output (-o) targets /dev/shm, /var/tmp or a hidden file in /tmp; compile-after-delivery keeps source rather than a binary on disk.
rules.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Compile After Delivery

rules.name: csc or vbc compiles into a user-writable path
rules.description: csc.exe, vbc.exe or jsc.exe invoked with an output in a temp, public or AppData path, typical of loader compilation.
rules.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Compile After Delivery

rules.name: System process name running outside its system directory
rules.description: An image named svchost, lsass, csrss, services, smss, winlogon, wininit or spoolsv runs from a path outside C:\Windows\System32 or SysWOW64.

rules.name: Process image with a document double extension
rules.description: The executable path ends in a document or image extension followed by an executable extension, e.g. invoice.pdf.exe.

rules.name: curl or wget uploads a local file to an IP-literal URL
rules.description: curl -T/--upload-file/--data-binary @file or -F file=@ to an http(s) IP host, exfiltration over an existing web channel.

rules.name: Upload to an anonymous file-drop service from the command line
rules.description: curl/wget/powershell posting a file to transfer.sh, file.io, gofile, bashupload, 0x0.st, temp.sh or pixeldrain.

rules.name: Cloud access token printed or token cache read
rules.description: az account get-access-token, gcloud auth print-access-token, aws sts get-session-token or reading ~/.azure/accessTokens.json, gcloud credentials.db. Tools and scripts do this too, so informational.

rules.name: Pass-the-hash style invocation
rules.description: sekurlsa::pth, xfreerdp /pth:, pth-winexe or an impacket -hashes LM:NT argument supplies an NTLM hash instead of a password.

rules.name: Static bearer or JWT supplied on a command line
rules.description: A JWT-shaped token (eyJ...) passed to curl/kubectl/az as a bearer, --token or --access-token argument: an application access token reused directly.
rules.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

rules.name: Recursive search for password strings in config or home trees
rules.description: grep/findstr/Select-String sweeping directories for password, passwd, secret or api_key strings.

rules.name: Search or dump of Group Policy Preferences cpassword
rules.description: findstr /s cpassword over SYSVOL or Get-GPPPassword, which recover reversible passwords stored in GPP XML.

rules.name: Gatekeeper disabled or quarantine attribute stripped
rules.description: spctl --master-disable or xattr removal of com.apple.quarantine from an app or download.

rules.name: Self-signed code-signing certificate created
rules.description: New-SelfSignedCertificate -Type CodeSigningCert or makecert with the code-signing EKU. Developers do this, so informational.

rules.name: Mark-of-the-Web removed
rules.description: Unblock-File, or deleting the Zone.Identifier stream, strips the download marker that triggers SmartScreen and Office protections.

rules.name: Driver-signing or system integrity enforcement disabled
rules.description: bcdedit testsigning/nointegritychecks on or loadoptions DDISABLE_INTEGRITY_CHECKS; csrutil disable.
rules.technique_name: Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing Policy Modification

rules.name: Core system binary written or replaced
rules.description: A write to sshd, ssh, sudo, login, passwd, su, ps, netstat, ss or lsof in a system binary directory; trojanized replacements keep persistence. Package managers also do this, so informational.

rules.name: Credential store extraction tool or command
rules.description: LaZagne, keepassxc-cli export, or secret-tool search --all read stored credentials in bulk.

rules.name: Windows Credential Manager enumerated
rules.description: cmdkey /list, vaultcmd /listcreds, keymgr.dll or Get-VaultCredential read stored Windows credentials.
rules.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager

rules.name: Cloud or cluster secret read from the command line
rules.description: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value, az keyvault secret show, gcloud secrets versions access, or kubectl get secret with output of the data.
rules.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores

rules.name: Kerberos ticket abuse tooling
rules.description: Rubeus kerberoast/asktgt/dump/tgtdeleg, Invoke-Kerberoast, GetUserSPNs.py or setspn -Q */* request or extract service tickets.

rules.name: Golden ticket forging command
rules.description: mimikatz kerberos::golden, ticketer.py with -domain-sid, or Rubeus golden.
rules.technique_name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket

positive.command: python3 ticketer.py -nthash abc -domain-sid S-1-5-21-1 -domain corp.local admin

rules.name: Password-protected archive created
rules.description: 7z a -p, rar a -hp or zip -P/-e over a directory, a common way to stage data so inspection fails. Users also encrypt archives, so informational.

rules.name: Raw disk or partition table overwrite
rules.description: dd/wipefs/sgdisk/diskpart clean targeting a whole disk device, which destroys partition structure.

rules.name: Windows event logging disabled
rules.description: auditpol /clear or disable, wevtutil sl /e:false, sc config eventlog start= disabled, or Stop-Service EventLog.
rules.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging

rules.name: Event tracing or sensor-driver blinding
rules.description: logman stop/delete of an ETW trace, fltmc unload of a sensor minifilter, COMPlus_ETWEnabled=0, or Set-EtwTraceProvider disabling providers.

rules.name: Cloud firewall or security group opened to the world
rules.description: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress, gcloud firewall-rules create/update, or az network nsg rule create with 0.0.0.0/0 or * source.
rules.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Firewall

positive.command: gcloud compute firewall-rules create open --source-ranges 0.0.0.0/0 --allow tcp:22

rules.name: SSH agent socket of another session used
rules.description: SSH_AUTH_SOCK is set to a /tmp/ssh-*/agent.* socket on the command line, using someone else's forwarded agent.
rules.technique_name: Remote Service Session Hijacking: SSH Hijacking

rules.name: tscon takes over another session
rules.description: tscon <id> /dest: moves another user's RDP session to the caller without credentials when run as SYSTEM.
rules.technique_name: Remote Service Session Hijacking: RDP Hijacking

rules.name: Files hidden through attributes
rules.description: attrib +h +s, chflags hidden or SetFile -a V applied to hide payloads or folders from default listings.

rules.name: Hidden user account created
rules.description: dscl IsHidden 1, SpecialAccounts\UserList value 0 via reg add, or Hide500Users set: a login account hidden from the login screen.

rules.name: Virtual machine started headless
rules.description: VBoxManage startvm --type headless, qemu with -nographic/-display none, or vmrun nogui; hidden VMs isolate malware from host tooling. Legitimate for servers and CI.

rules.name: Download from a dynamic-DNS hostname
rules.description: curl/wget/powershell fetching from duckdns, no-ip, ddns.net, hopto.org, zapto.org or serveo, whose records are cheap to rotate.

rules.name: Unsigned commonly hijacked DLL loaded from a user-writable directory
rules.description: An unsigned version, winmm, dbghelp, cryptsp, wtsapi32, dwmapi, ntmarta or wlbsctrl DLL loads from AppData, Temp, ProgramData or Public, the search-order and sideloading pattern.

rules.name: Known phantom DLL created in a system directory
rules.description: A file named wlbsctrl, ualapi, tsmsisrv, ikeext, cdpsgshims or diagtrack_win dll is created in System32/SysWOW64, planting a DLL a service looks for.

rules.name: DYLD library injection environment set
rules.description: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH set to a /tmp, /Users/Shared, or user-writable path in a command line, dylib hijacking or injection.

rules.name: DNS zone transfer or enumeration tool
rules.description: dig/host/nslookup requesting AXFR, or dnsrecon/dnsenum/fierce/amass/subfinder enumeration.

rules.name: Serverless function created or code replaced
rules.description: aws lambda create-function/update-function-code, az functionapp deployment, gcloud functions deploy from a shell. Routine for developers, so informational.

rules.name: IIS native module or handler installed
rules.description: appcmd install module/add module with an image, or New-WebGlobalModule registers a native DLL in the web server, a web-server persistence route.

rules.name: Credential-dumping toolkit invoked by name
rules.description: secretsdump.py, pypykatz, nanodump, lsassy, mimipenguin or similar dumpers named on a command line.

rules.name: Privilege-elevation configuration tampered with
rules.description: A NOPASSWD sudoers line appended, setcap granting cap_setuid/cap_sys_admin, or a UAC-bypass ms-settings/mscfile shell\open\command key written with reg add.

rules.name: Signed binary used to fetch and run remote content
rules.description: msiexec /i with a URL, ieexec with a URL, syncappvpublishingserver or pubprn.vbs with a URL: signed-binary proxy execution from a remote source.

rules.name: systemd-run creates a transient timer
rules.description: systemd-run with a calendar or boot timer option schedules recurring execution without leaving a unit file on disk.

rules.name: shred or srm of a hidden file in a temp directory
rules.description: A secure-delete tool removes a dot-file from /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm, the pattern of an implant erasing itself.

rules.name: Command-line HTTP client posing as an obsolete Internet Explorer
rules.description: curl or wget sets a MSIE 4 to 8 user agent, a long-lived habit of commodity beacons and droppers.

rules.name: PowerShell WebClient with a custom Cookie or Authorization header to a raw IP
rules.description: A WebClient sets a Cookie or Authorization header and then fetches from a bare IP address, the shape of a scripted HTTP beacon.

rules.name: ssh reuses a control socket stored in a temp directory
rules.description: ssh -S points at a multiplex control socket under /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm, the way an attacker rides another user's authenticated session.
rules.technique_name: Remote Service Session Hijacking: SSH Hijacking

rules.name: Winlogon SpecialAccounts UserList value written
rules.description: A value under Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList hides that account from the logon screen.

rules.name: Unsigned DLL carrying a hijack-prone system name loaded from an application folder
rules.description: An unsigned module named like a Windows system DLL (version, winmm, cryptsp, dwmapi and similar) loads from outside the Windows directories, the classic search-order hijack.
rules.technique_name: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Search Order Hijacking

rules.name: Unsigned shared object or dylib loaded from a world-writable directory
rules.description: An unsigned library loads from /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm or /Users/Shared, a dylib or shared-object hijack staging area.
